entities.label: TextOfTheConstitution
entities.rationale: The text of the Constitution is a specific information artifact — a pattern of content that can be instantiated on paper, in digital form, or recited orally. It is not tied to any single physical substrate; it is a generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031). It is an individual (this specific constitutional text), and fits under the existing working class Statute (itself typed as BFO_0000031). The already-existing individual USConstitution appears to refer to the constitutional document as a whole (potentially conflating document and text); TextOfTheConstitution specifically denotes the linguistic/normative content — the pattern that is copied across substrates.

relations.rationale: The text of the Constitution is an instance of the Statute class, which is already typed as BFO_0000031 (Generically dependent continuant), capturing its nature as a copyable normative information content.

The text is part of (BFO_0000050) the US Constitution individual, which represents the constitutional document as a whole. The textual content is a proper part of that broader generically dependent continuant.

open_questions: Should 'USConstitution' be re-typed or refined to distinguish the physical/institutional document from its textual content, or is USConstitution intended to denote the text specifically?
Is 'the text of the Constitution' meant to refer to the US Constitution specifically, or to constitutional text in general (in which case it should be a class, not an individual)?
Should TextOfTheConstitution be modeled as a subtype of both Statute and a more specific class like ConstitutionalText (not yet in the ontology)?
proposal.rationale_summary: The text of the Constitution is paradigmatically a generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031): it is an information pattern — the linguistic and normative content — that can be multiply instantiated across physical bearers (printed documents, screens, oral recitations) without being identical to any one of them. It is an individual (this specific text), not a class. The most appropriate existing class is working:Statute (already BFO_0000031). A part-of relation to working:USConstitution is proposed, though an open question is raised about whether USConstitution already conflates the document-as-object with its textual content, which would need resolution to avoid redundancy or inconsistency.
